useIndex.description:
If True, then the indices of `targetOutput`, `modelOutput`, and `context` are used for score
calculation.

batchSize.description:
If the provided data does not fit in memory, then use this value as batch size to iterate through and compute incremental
metrics on batches of data.

normalization.description: Normalization to apply to the score. No normalization is applied if the field is empty.

title:
Root Mean Squared Error metric computes the squared root of the average squared error between
predicted value and target value:

$\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N (y_i-\hat{y}_i)^2}$

The metric is primarily used for regression problems and is very sensitive to outliers.

RMSE is unnormalized, and is thus dependent on the scale of the target variable. To compare the metric
values across different datasets, the metric can be normalized to obtain Normalized RMSE (NRMSE), defined as

$\text{NRMSE} = \frac{\text{RMSE}}{x}$

where $x$ is the normalizing factor computed on the target value. See
{@link MlRootMeanSquaredErrorMetric.Normalization} for available options for normalizing factor $x$.

The `modelOutput` and `targetOutput` are expected to have the same shape.
This metric supports `sampleWeights` as `context`. `sampleWeights` is single-dimensional with same number of samples
as the `modelOutput`. It represents a per-sample weighting when aggregating for RMSE calculation.
name: MlRootMeanSquaredErrorMetric
